cards.back: A whole number greater than 1 with exactly two factors: 1 and itself. Example: 13.
cards.say: What is a prime number? A whole number greater than one with exactly two factors: one and itself. Example: thirteen.

cards.back: No. 1 has only one factor (itself), and a prime needs exactly two.
cards.say: Is one a prime number? No. One has only one factor, itself, and a prime needs exactly two.

cards.back: 2. Every other even number can be divided by 2, so it has more than two factors.
cards.say: The only even prime number. Two. Every other even number can be divided by two, so it has more than two factors.
Primes up to twenty. Two, three, five, seven, eleven, thirteen, seventeen, nineteen
Primes between twenty and thirty. Twenty three and twenty nine

cards.back: No. 51 = 3 × 17, so it has more factors than 1 and 51. (Its digits add to 6, so 3 goes into it.)
cards.say: Is fifty one prime? No. Fifty one equals three times seventeen, so it has more factors than one and fifty one. Its digits add to six, so three goes into it.
Is ninety one prime? No. Ninety one equals seven times thirteen.

cards.back: Yes. It cannot be divided by 2, 3, 5 or 7, so it has no other factors.
cards.say: Is ninety seven prime? Yes. It cannot be divided by two, three, five or seven, so it has no other factors.

cards.back: A whole number greater than 1 that has more than two factors. Example: 12.
cards.say: What is a composite number? A whole number greater than one that has more than two factors. Example: twelve.
Factors of twelve. One, two, three, four, six, twelve
Factors of thirty. One, two, three, five, six, ten, fifteen, thirty
Factors of thirty six. One, two, three, four, six, nine, twelve, eighteen, thirty six
Factor pairs of twenty four. One times twenty four, two times twelve, three times eight, four times six
First five multiples of seven. Seven, fourteen, twenty one, twenty eight, thirty five
Is fifty six a multiple of eight? Yes. Eight times seven equals fifty six.

cards.back: 1, 2, 3 and 6. The highest common factor (HCF) is 6.
cards.say: Common factors of twelve and eighteen. One, two, three and six. The highest common factor, HCF, is six.

cards.back: 10. It is the biggest number that goes into both 20 and 30.
cards.say: Highest common factor of twenty and thirty. Ten. It is the biggest number that goes into both twenty and thirty.

cards.back: 12. Multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12. Multiples of 6: 6, 12. The first match is 12.
cards.say: Lowest common multiple of four and six. Twelve. Multiples of four: four, eight, twelve. Multiples of six: six, twelve. The first match is twelve.

cards.back: 15, because 3 and 5 share no factor except 1, so multiply: 3 × 5 = 15.
cards.say: Lowest common multiple of three and five. Fifteen, because three and five share no factor except one, so multiply them.
Which of twenty one, twenty three, twenty five, twenty seven is prime? Twenty three. The others are three times seven, five times five and three times nine.

cards.front: A number that is a factor of every whole number
cards.back: 1. Every whole number can be divided by 1.
cards.say: A number that is a factor of every whole number. One. Every whole number can be divided by one.

cards.front: True or false: a square number has an odd number of factors
cards.back: True. Example: 36 has 9 factors. Factors pair up, but the square root pairs with itself.
cards.say: True or false: a square number has an odd number of factors. True. Example: thirty six has nine factors. Factors pair up, but the square root pairs with itself.
